question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the storage characteristics from the left onto the storage types on the right.
bank: moderately expensive and simple to configure
most resilient, highly scalable, and high-performance storage
lacks scalability, performance, and advanced features
theory: SAN (block-level, Fibre Channel/FCoE-based) storage is generally the most resilient, highly scalable, and highest-performing option, but it is also the most expensive and complex to design, zone, and manage. NAS is a simpler, moderately priced file-access appliance that presents shared file systems directly to hosts over Ethernet/IP, trading some of SAN's raw scalability and advanced feature set for lower cost and easier configuration. Recognizing this cost/complexity-versus-performance trade-off is the core exam concept behind comparing NAS and SAN. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 10 - NAS Concepts)
